sources.name: GDP GROWTH
sources.label: Quarterly economic output, YoY
sources.description: Quarterly GDP growth, year-on-year. Headline GDP is increasingly defense-spending-led; the civilian economy looks weaker than the topline implies.
sources.whyItMatters: Headline GDP is now defense-spending-led; the civilian economy looks worse than the topline implies.

sources.name: INFLATION RATE
sources.label: Consumer Price Index, YoY
sources.description: Monthly headline CPI, year-on-year. Real purchasing power has lagged official inflation since Q3 2022 — wages have not kept up.
sources.whyItMatters: Wages have lagged official inflation since Q3 2022 — this is the best proxy for how a salary feels at the supermarket.

sources.name: SENTIMENT SCORE
sources.label: Public-search and news-tone proxy
sources.description: Indirect sentiment proxy from Google Trends queries on Russian-language hardship terms (relocation, prices, mobilisation). Scored 0–100 (100 = fully positive).
sources.whyItMatters: Public surveys are unreliable in autocracies; search behaviour is harder to fake.

sources.name: PUBLIC POLLS
sources.label: Independent life-satisfaction polling
sources.description: Levada Center's life-satisfaction composite. Levada is one of the few polling outlets still publishing despite "foreign agent" pressure.
sources.whyItMatters: Levada is the closest thing to independent polling left inside Russia — readers and policymakers cite it.

sources.name: EMIGRATION INDEX
sources.label: Monthly departures (thousands)
sources.description: Estimated monthly outflow combining Eurostat first-time asylum applications by Russian citizens with residency-permit data from Georgia and Armenia.
sources.whyItMatters: When educated workers leave faster than they're replaced, long-term economic capacity erodes regardless of headline numbers.

sources.name: NEWS NEGATIVITY
sources.label: Negative-tone share of Russia events
sources.description: Share of negative-tone Russia events on the GDELT 2.0 Goldstein scale, monthly average. Captures how state and global media frame Russia.
sources.whyItMatters: When state outlets emphasise fear and conflict, it tends to lead internal mobilisation or repression cycles.

sources.name: ROSSTAT GAP
sources.label: Official vs. independent estimate divergence
sources.description: Multiplier between Rosstat figures and independent estimates from BOFIT (Bank of Finland) and Yale CELI. Higher = greater statistical opacity.
sources.whyItMatters: When official numbers diverge from independent estimates, the official narrative is harder to take at face value.

sources.name: ECON. FREEDOM
sources.label: Heritage Foundation index, 0–100
sources.description: Heritage Foundation Economic Freedom score. Russia ranked 162nd globally in the 2024 release. Tracks property rights, government integrity, trade freedom.
sources.whyItMatters: Property rights and trade freedom are slow-moving structural metrics — they signal long-run trajectory, not month-to-month noise.

sources.name: RUBLE / USD
sources.label: Daily exchange rate, ₽ per $1
sources.description: USD/RUB rate at month-close. The 2022 spike reflects sanctions shock; later stabilisation came from capital controls and forced export-revenue conversion.
sources.whyItMatters: The ruble is the only daily-published indicator the Russian state can't easily massage — it's a real-time confidence vote.
